title: Building With a Sword at Hand
overview: As Jerusalem's wall goes up, neighboring leaders mock and then threaten the builders, and Nehemiah organizes the people to keep working while staying ready to defend themselves.

parts.label: Mockery from the neighbors (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Sanballat, a leading official in Samaria to the north, sneers in front of his allies and troops that these weak Jews can never finish quickly or bring burned stones back from rubble. His ally Tobiah adds that even a fox would knock the wall down, a pointed joke since foxes were known to roam the city's ruins.

parts.label: An angry prayer, then progress (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Nehemiah does not answer the insults but asks God to turn the shame back on the mockers and not forgive them, a raw prayer for punishment that the text records without comment. Meanwhile the work, split into sections around the city, reaches half the wall's planned height because the people put their whole heart into it.

parts.label: A plot and tired workers (vv. 7-12)
parts.note: Enemies on every side, from Samaria, Ammon, Arabia and the coastal city of Ashdod, plan a surprise attack, while the builders themselves say they are worn out and the rubble is endless. Jews living near the enemy warn Nehemiah again and again, though the exact wording of their message in verse 12 is unclear in the original language.

parts.label: Nehemiah arms the families (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: He posts people by family groups with weapons at the lowest, most exposed spots and tells them to remember God and fight for their homes and loved ones. Once the enemy learns the plan is known, the attack falls apart and everyone goes back to building.

parts.label: Working ready for attack (vv. 16-21)
parts.note: From then on half the men stand guard while the rest build with a weapon close at hand, from first light until the stars come out. A trumpeter stays beside Nehemiah so that, with the workers spread far apart, everyone can rush to any point that is attacked.

parts.label: Guarding through the night (vv. 22-23)
parts.note: Nehemiah tells every worker and his helper to stay inside Jerusalem at night so they can guard by night and build by day. He and his brothers, his men and his guards never take off their clothes, and each keeps his weapon even when going for water.

think: When something you care about is mocked or threatened, what keeps you going, and what makes you want to give up?
